cards.title: Introduction to Data Binding
cards.content:
Data binding in Vue.js allows you to connect your component's state (JavaScript data) to the rendered DOM (HTML).

Vue uses a reactive data binding system, meaning when the data changes, the UI updates automatically.

cards.title: Text Interpolation with Mustaches
cards.content:
The most basic form of data binding is text interpolation using the "Mustache" syntax (double curly braces).

<template>
  <p>Message: {{ message }}</p>
</template>

<script>
export default {
  data() {
    return {
      message: 'Hello Vue!'
    }
  }
}
</script>

cards.title: Attribute Binding with v-bind
cards.content:
Mustaches cannot be used inside HTML attributes. To bind an attribute to dynamic data, use the v-bind directive.

<img v-bind:src="imageSrc" alt="Dynamic Image">

Vue provides a shorthand for v-bind: simply use a colon (:).

<img :src="imageSrc" alt="Dynamic Image">

content.text: To use the shorthand syntax for v-bind:src, you write it as ___src="imageSrc".

cards.title: Two-Way Data Binding with v-model
cards.content:
While v-bind is one-way (from state to view), the v-model directive creates two-way data binding on form input, textarea, and select elements.

<input v-model="searchText" placeholder="Search..." />
<p>Searching for: {{ searchText }}</p>

It automatically syncs the input value with the JavaScript state.

cards.title: Match Vue Directives to their Purpose
Order the Steps of Setting Up a Reactive Component

items: Define the data property in the component's data option
Include the reactive variable in the template using interpolation or directives
Update the data property via methods or user input
Observe the UI automatically re-render with the new value

cards.title: Data Binding Summary
cards.content:
Great job! You've learned the core concepts of Vue.js data binding:

  • Text Interpolation ({{ }}) for rendering text.
  • v-bind (:) for dynamic HTML attributes.
  • v-model for two-way input binding.
